newsitem.title: USA: CME March lumber closes up limit on cash ideas.
newsitem.headline: CME March lumber closes up limit on cash ideas.

text.p: Expectations of firming cash markets kept CME March lumber futures up the daily limit of $10.00 per tbf at the close, with other months following on spillover demand, traders said.
March closed limit up at $415.80 and May up $8.60 at $390.60 per tbf after also being up the limit earlier. Other months finished up $4.50 to $2.40 higher.

March led the rally on demand prompted by warmer weather forecasts and expectations that cash lumber prices will start their seasonal rise soon. Buy stops were hit in thin dealings and prices ran up the daily limit, traders said.
"The market is up more on speculation of higher cash than on actual gains in cash prices," one trader said.
Adding to expectations of firmer cash was the Supreme Court's denial of a timber company's appeal to log Douglas fir in an old-growth forest in California, analysts said.

The Court denied an appeal by a MAXXAM Inc unit to log because of the marbled murrelet, a seabird that breeds in old-growth forests in California. The murrelet has been listed by the federal government as a threatened, not an endangered, species, along the Pacific Coast.
